feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy Guide
feeds.description: Cerebral Palsy Guide provides free educational materials, financial options, and emotional support for those affected by cerebral palsy. It is our mission to create an easy-to-use, informative website that provides solutions for families. It is our hope that the Cerebral Palsy Guide can help parents of children with cerebral palsy find peace, healing, and happiness.

feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy Guidance
feeds.description: We provide vital guidance and assistance to parents of a child with cerebral palsy. Information on causes, treatment, financial assistance, and more. Our goal is to reach as many members of the cerebral palsy community as possible, build up a network of support, as well as providing necessary assistance.

feeds.title: ScienceDaily News » Cerebral Palsy
feeds.description: Read about the latest research into cerebral palsy, including risk factors and experimental treatments on ScienceDaily

feeds.title: News Medical » Cerebral Palsy News
feeds.description: Get the Latest Cerebral Palsy News and Research from around the world on News Medical

feeds.title: Disability Scoop » Cerebral Palsy
feeds.description: Here you can view the latest cerebral palsy news from treatment and therapy to parenting and caregiving, education, advocacy, research and more. Founded in 2008, Disability Scoop is the nation's largest news organization devoted to covering developmental disabilities.

feeds.title: UCP of Greater Cleveland Blog
feeds.description: The mission of UCP of Greater Cleveland is to empower children and adults with disabilities to advance their independence, productivity and inclusion in the community.

feeds.title: Hannah's Adventures of Living Her Dreams
feeds.description: My name is Hannah Thompson. I recently graduated from Elmhurst College with a B.A. in Communication. I am a motivational speaker encouraging people to do their impossible. I was born with Cerebral Palsy and that does not stop me from doing anything! I am changing the world one audience at a time!

feeds.title: Aideen Blackborough
feeds.description: I have Cerebral Palsy but it doesn't have me!

feeds.title: My Cerebral Palsy Child Blog
feeds.description: MyCerebralPalsyChild.org is a web-based help center where parents can learn more about cerebral palsy - its history, causes, symptoms, treatments, and the future of cerebral palsy research. Here you can learn about how cerebral palsy impacts the everyday lives of everyone - from babies, children, and adults, to the people in their lives dedicated to helping them deal with the challenges of everyday life.

feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy News Today
feeds.description: Cerebral Palsy News Today is committed to presenting the CP community with the latest science, health, and advocacy news related to Cerebral Palsy.

feeds.title: Love That Max
feeds.description: Love That Max is a blog by Ellen Seidman, Max's mom, who writes about her life raising her son with cerebral palsy, as well as many other things.

feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy Foundation Blog
feeds.description: The Cerebral Palsy Foundation is dedicated to transforming lives for people with cerebral palsy today through research, innovation, and collaboration.

feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy Blog
feeds.description: Pooya Hosseinzadeh, MD, the author of this blog, is a pediatric orthopedic physician at Washington University Orthopedics in St. Louis, Missouri. He specializes in the evaluation and treatment of neuromuscular conditions in children, including cerebral palsy. This blog was created to discuss the operative and non-operative treatments that are available for certain musculoskeletal conditions in children with cerebral palsy

feeds.title: Zachary Fenell Blog
feeds.description: Online home for Zachary Fenell, author, public speaker, and all around cerebral palsy advocate!

feeds.title: View From a Walking Frame
feeds.description: A blog about an average girl who just happens to have Cerebral Palsy

feeds.title: Life as a Cerebral Palsy student
feeds.description: Hi! My name is Chloe Tear, I am 19 years old and I'm a university student studying Psychology and Child Development. I have mild cerebral palsy which affects the left side of my body as a result of being born 8 weeks early and weighing 3lb 3oz, as well as epilepsy, chronic pain and impaired vision. feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy Law Doctor Blog
feeds.description: Our team is uniquely qualified with both Legal and Medical degrees, which is why we are the choice of so many parents seeking justice for their child with Cerebral Palsy and why others with serious and permanent injuries due to medical mistakes seek out our counsel.

feeds.title: Living with Cerebral Palsy
feeds.description: Hello! My name is Evie, I am sixteen years old and I have Spastic Cerebral Palsy. I am writing this blog to raise awareness about Cerebral Palsy and Epilepsy and discuss topics which often just aren't talked about

feeds.title: Mum Making Lemonade
feeds.description: A blog about my amazing daughter, Elin who is living with Cerebral Palsy and making Lemonade every day!

feeds.title: Our So Called CP Life
feeds.description: It was Thanksgiving day back in 2002. I was only 23 years old and my life forever changed on that day. I had a placental abruption and Brendan was born at 33 weeks. He lost oxygen during delivery due to incompetent care but was a fighter and turned 13 this year. My journey in life over the past 13 years took many turns I was not expecting but I try to stay strong and have my husband by my side even when I am not.

feeds.title: Tonia Says
feeds.description: Tonia Says is my take on life with CP, C-PTSD and being neurodivergent. It's my ultimate goal to make this blog a space where disabled people can come and know that we are safe, loved and fully seen.

feeds.title: My Life As Brittney
feeds.description: Welcome to my little piece of the internet. Spoonie. Spastic Diplegia Cerebral Palsy. Chronic blog. INFJ. Aries. Open inbox.

feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy Research Network Blog
feeds.description: Cerebral Palsy Daily Living is designed to give families and caregivers dealing with CP a central place for practical information and resources within the context of an emotionally-supportive community.

feeds.title: Cerebral Palsy Strong
feeds.description: Welcome to Cerebral Palsy Strong! My name is Katy Fetters & I started CPstrong in order to sustain my existence in the online space long after my blog for teens with cerebral palsy fell behind as I entered into adulthood. Most importantly, I want to have a place where I can share stories about myself, others, and our experiences of life [in our 20's] with cerebral palsy.
